chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

A child of one of the companions of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام died, and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام attended. When he was placed into the niche-grave, his father came forward to throw earth upon him, so Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام took hold of his hands.
And he said: “Do not throw earth upon him, and whoever among his relatives is of kinship to him should not throw earth upon him.”

We said: “O son of the Messenger of Allah, are you forbidding only him from this?” He said: “I forbid you from throwing earth upon close relatives, for that causes hardness in the heart, and whoever’s heart becomes hard grows distant from his Lord.”

key_terms.أُلْحِدَ: was placed into the grave niche
key_terms.التُّرَابَ: the earth or soil thrown over the grave
key_terms.الْقَلْبِ: the heart, understood spiritually and morally

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام forbid relatives from throwing soil on the grave of their family member?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام forbade close relatives from throwing soil onto the grave of their deceased kin. The stated reason is ethical and spiritual: such an act may produce hardness in the heart, and hardness of heart distances a person from Allah.
